findings.issue: Identical not-found boilerplate (setTitle('Not found – Pokédex') + RESPONSE_INIT 404) is duplicated in all four detail resolvers and again in not-found-view.ts:13-16
findings.suggestion: Extract a `resolvePage(fetch)` helper or `setNotFound(titleService, responseInit)` util so 404 behavior changes in one place

findings.issue: The '– Pokédex' title suffix is duplicated in 10 call sites across resolvers and components
findings.suggestion: Add a `setPageTitle(heading: string)` helper in util (or the same resolver helper) and route all title setting through it

findings.issue: CardEntry construction and dex ordering duplicated between home.pageEntries and PokedexData.cardsFor (pokedex-data.ts:127-141)
findings.suggestion: Have home feed species refs through a shared entry-builder (or document the split) so ordering/formatting changes have one home

findings.issue: Move field mapping (english name, type label, category, power/accuracy/pp) overlaps with move.resolver.ts:40-46's description-list mapping
findings.suggestion: Extract a `moveFacts(move, typeNames)` helper shared by both resolvers

findings.issue: Type-name-to-English lookup (typeNames.get(x) ?? humanize(x)) repeated in four places
findings.suggestion: Add a `typeLabel(name): {name, english}` helper on PokedexData

findings.issue: Caching spans three layers: Api's promise cache, PokedexData's memoized dataset promises (pokedex-data.ts:33-70), and the HTTP transfer cache (app.config.ts:19)
findings.suggestion: Fine as-is, but centralize cache policy (TTL, invalidation) in Api and have PokedexData delegate, so a caching-rule change touches one file

findings.issue: The 'level-up' method name is hardcoded to decide whether the Level column shows
findings.suggestion: Carry a `hasLevel` boolean on MoveTable from the resolver instead of string-matching the method in the template

summary: A well-factored Angular 22 app: every page is a self-contained route/resolver/component trio, data flows through two narrow services, and card rendering and the trickiest business rule (Pokémon-ref → species mapping) are each centralized in one reusable place. The costs are small but real: resolver boilerplate (titles, 404 status) is copy-pasted across four files, and a couple of mapping helpers are repeated rather than extracted. Changes land in one obvious place for data and display logic, and in a handful of greppable spots for cross-cutting concerns.
